newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian oil imports to slow after fire at port.
newsitem.headline: Zambian oil imports to slow after fire at port.

text.p: Zambian oil imports are likely to slow over the next few weeks after a fire damaged an offloading facility at the port of Dar-es-Salaam in neighbouring Tanzania, the ministry of energy said on Tuesday.
Energy minister Suresh Desai said the accident occurred on Christmas Day, killing five people, as Tanzanian Habours Authority workers were carrying out repairs.
"An explosive fire caused by an oil spill occured during repairing. The fire engulfed the whole facility and led to the death of five men," Desai told reporters.
The minister said the would be no fuel shortages or price hikes because of the accident.

"Until the SPM (single point mooring) is brought back into full operation, crude oil will be brought in small ships to ease handling through the alternative smaller off-loading facility. There is, therefore, no need for worry," he said.
He said the Tanzanian authorities expected repairs at the offloading facility to take about a month.
Asked why it had taken the governmment two weeks to disclose the problem, Desai said it had been awaiting "a full report" from Tanzania.
Last year, Zambia was forced to import petroluem products from her neighbours to cover a shortfall resulting from maintenance problems at Dar-es-Salaam.
Zambian supplies of crude oil were marooned at the port for two months while repair works were being carried out at the port.
